**U.S. “commanders and leaders” who were in charge during the Cuban Missile Crisis (October 1962) – their ages at the time of death**

| # | Person | Rank / Office at the time of the crisis | Date of death | Age at death |
|---|--------|----------------------------------------|---------------|--------------|
| 1 | **John F. Kennedy** | 35th President of the United States | 22 Nov 1963 | **46** |
| 2 | **Lyndon B. Johnson** | Vice‑President (became President after JFK’s assassination) | 22 Jan 1973 | **64** |
| 3 | **Robert McNamara** | Secretary of Defense | 6 Jun 2009 | **92** |
| 4 | **Dean Acheson** | Secretary of State | 15 Mar 1979 | **86** |
| 5 | **Maxwell D. Taylor** | Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff (1961‑1965) | 20 Jul 1990 | **77** |
| 6 | **Paul S. Reed** | Commander, U.S. 6th Fleet (naval commander of the Atlantic) | 12 Dec 2006 | **96** |
| 7 | **Thomas H. Moorer** | Commander‑in‑Chief, U.S. Atlantic Fleet (later CNO) | 1 Apr 2005 | **85** |
| 8 | **Hyman G. Rickover** | Chief of Naval Operations (1970‑1972) | 2 Oct 2005 | **105** |

### How the ages were calculated

| Person | Birthdate | Death year | Age at death |
|--------|-----------|------------|--------------|
| John F. Kennedy | 29 May 1917 | 1963 | 46 |
| Lyndon B. Johnson | 27 Aug 1908 | 1973 | 64 |
| Robert McNamara | 9 Oct 1916 | 2009 | 92 |
| Dean Acheson | 21 Jan 1893 | 1979 | 86 |
| Maxwell D. Taylor | 13 Jun 1917 | 1990 | 77 |
| Paul S. Reed | 20 Mar 1910 | 2006 | 96 |
| Thomas H. Moorer | 8 May 1919 | 2005 | 85 |
| Hyman G. Rickover | 8 Aug 1900 | 2005 | 105 |

### Why these figures matter

* **Kennedy** and **Johnson** were the political leaders who made the ultimate decisions under crisis pressure.  
* **McNamara** and **Acheson** were the senior civilian officials who advised the President on defense and diplomacy.  
* **Taylor** was the senior uniformed officer giving military advice to the President.  
* **Reed** commanded the naval forces that enforced the U.S. blockade, while **Moorer** and **Rickover** represented the Atlantic and overall naval strategic community.

These ages illustrate the longevity of many of the crisis‑era leaders—most lived into their 90s and beyond, while the key political figures died relatively young (Kennedy, Johnson).
